text:
Ah, the primary material of a candle. It is, of course, wax. Specifically, the paraffin-based tears of the petroleum industry, molded into a cylindrical monument to our collective inability to function without a flickering light source while we doom-scroll through our existential dread.

Welcome to adulthood, where the "magical journey" is less *Harry Potter* and more *The Office* if everyone was constantly on the verge of a nervous breakdown. You are now a fully functioning adult, which is just a fancy way of saying you have mastered the art of pretending you know what you’re doing while internally screaming because you forgot to buy toilet paper.

Spontaneity? Please. In the grand theater of your new life, spontaneity is merely the thrill of choosing between "Chicken" and "Beef" instant noodles, a decision so profound it requires a full three minutes of boiling water and a moment of silence to appreciate the complexity of your palate. And long-term planning? Oh, the sheer ambition! You are now strategizing the next four hours of your life with the precision of a military general, deciding whether to watch *The Office* for the 400th time or finally start that documentary about deep-sea squids that you will definitely not finish.

It is a life of high stakes, low rewards, and the constant, nagging suspicion that your back pain is not just "growing pains" but a permanent subscription service you can’t cancel. Enjoy the wax.
